the following questions: (i) How does the implicit regularizer induced by data augmentation relate to the classical L2 and L1 norms?
the following questions: 1) What is the implicit regularization imposed by data augmentation? 2) What is the effect of data augmentation in terms of the generalization error?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the implicit regularization of deep learning is a form of data-dependent regularization that is not based on the Hessian of the loss function.
the implicit regularization effect of data augmentation is to penalize the roughness of the function being learned by the neural network.

“The use of data augmentation in deep neural network models is a form of implicit regularization that penalizes the roughness of the function learned by the model, and that the use of data augmentation is equivalent to adding a regularizing term to the loss function that penalizes the function’s roughness.”
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the implicit rugosity regularization induced by data augmentation can improve generalization, but it can also be detrimental to the training if the data augmentation scheme is too aggressive, leading to over-smoothing.
we have developed a method to quantify how much a function is smooth or “bumpy” and we have found a way to use this to improve the performance of a neural network.
we propose a new implicit regularizer for deep networks that can be interpreted geometrically and can be computed efficiently via the data augmentation heuristic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
data augmentation is a powerful tool that can be used to improve the generalization of deep neural networks by controlling their roughness.
data augmentation implicitly regularizes the function space by penalizing the rugosity of the function fit.
the implicit regularizer induced by data augmentation is a proxy for the roughness of the function being fit.
